text:
Recommendation: Offer annual billing at $490/year; don't skip it.
Why:
- 40 customers (13% of your base) explicitly asked for it, signaling intent to stay and possibly a procurement need for annual invoicing.
- The apparent $98 discount per switcher only holds if that customer would have stayed all 12 months on monthly. If monthly churn is above roughly 3.3%, annual billing yields more expected revenue per customer than monthly, before counting the value of upfront cash. At 2% churn, expected monthly revenue is ~$530; at 3.3%, ~$490 (break-even); at 5%, ~$450.
- If all 40 switch, that's roughly $19.6k collected upfront instead of trickling in over the year.
- "Two months free" on an annual plan is standard SaaS pricing (roughly 15-20% off), not a brand-cheapening discount; that reputation risk applies to frequent or random price cuts, not a permanent annual option.
Risks and unknowns:
- Customers who would have stayed 12+ months anyway now pay $98 less; this true cost depends on your actual churn rate.
- Need a refund policy for mid-year cancellations (e.g., no refunds, access continues until term ends).
- Annual customers won't see a price increase until renewal.
Next steps:
1. Check your current monthly churn rate to see whether it's above the ~3.3% break-even threshold.
2. As a reversible test, email the 490 annual option to the 40 who asked (and possibly the full customer base) before adding it to the public pricing page.
3. Track uptake and churn over the following months, then decide whether to make it a permanent, publicly listed option (setup is about a day via Stripe).
